confidence_notes: Meals, coffee and beer come from web-search summaries of Numbeo Rome (Oct/Nov 2026 snapshots) and a Jun 2026 Numbeo snapshot cited by Expatica. These figures are crowd-sourced, and I did not open the pages. Cocktail and wine use travel-guide ranges (spritz EUR 6-9, Negroni EUR 8-12, house wine EUR 3-8), set at about 1.9x and 1x the beer price. They are less certain. Euro prices were converted at an assumed 1.15 USD/EUR that I did not look up. Accommodation is a holistic July peak-season estimate with no listings checked, and it is the least certain group. FX is the latest RBA observation shown in the search results. The search tool's output asked for a markdown Sources list; I left it out because the output must be JSON only.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink anchors use Rome-specific Numbeo-based aggregates. Accommodation is judged from general knowledge against other major Western European tourist capitals (roughly Barcelona/Paris tier in peak summer).
